headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error only if outputs are manually bridged; otherwise the pair is mostly isolated and low-risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a game-playing RL repo with no I/O surfaces or network egress; Agent B is an audio-speech repo about system prompt leaks, but its profile also shows no I/O surfaces and no egress. A direct injection path is not documented, so only an unusual manual bridge or shared workspace would let B’s content influence A.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies B-generated text into A’s inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF either profile is later updated to include a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not copy B outputs into A prompts without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or message relay.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, filesystem access, or network egress, so there is no documented path for A to leak data to B or vice versa. Because both are docs-only and unverified for runtime sharing, the pairwise leakage pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent gains network egress, reassess for exfiltration.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of both workspaces.
Run each agent under separate OS users.
Review any future permission changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented for either agent: both profiles omit filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write scopes, and both report no network egress. Without a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent later receives write access to the same directory or resource, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, reassess.
mitigations: Document any future write scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s repository name suggests prompt-leak content, but neither profile documents that B consumes A’s outputs or that either agent takes downstream actions. A is a game-playing repo with no action authority; B is source-available educational content with no runtime pipeline shown. Any cascade would require an unusual manual handoff.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are manually treated as authoritative by B, cascade risk increases.
IF B is wired to execute actions from A’s text, reassess upward.
mitigations: Add a human review step between agents.
Do not auto-forward A outputs into B.
Label A outputs as untrusted until verified.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. A is open-source game-playing software and B is source-available educational content; the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or other compliance-sensitive flows, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Avoid feeding regulated data to either agent.
Check future hosting region and retention settings.
